question: Should Crabbox own and publish a first-party Herdr integration that adds a Herdr-specific hidden CLI compatibility surface?
rationale: Repository policy favors a generic core, while this branch creates ongoing compatibility and release obligations for an external workflow host; only maintainers can choose that ownership boundary.

options.title: External plugin, generic core
options.body: Keep the Herdr manifest and adapter in an external Herdr package and extract only any necessary stable, provider-neutral Crabbox CLI capability into a narrow PR.

options.title: Sponsor first-party Herdr
options.body: Accept first-party ownership, coordinate the merge with a compatible Crabbox release and marketplace topic, and require live proof plus explicit supported Herdr versions.

options.title: Pause the integration
options.body: Leave the PR open or close it without landing until there is a clear owner and demand for maintaining the external compatibility contract.

recommendation.title: External plugin, generic core
recommendation.body: Keep the Herdr manifest and adapter in an external Herdr package and extract only any necessary stable, provider-neutral Crabbox CLI capability into a narrow PR.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice spans Crabbox product scope, plugin ownership, repository metadata, and release sequencing.
